notable_absence.finding: This release-notes page spans roughly six years and dozens of point releases (3.0 through 3.12), and contains far more deprecatedIn/removedIn-shaped bug-fix and API-churn entries than were captured here (e.g. JCBC-1625 maxTTL->maxExpiry, JCBC-1647 EjectionPolicy->EvictionPolicyType, JVMCBC-1579 NodeIdentifier package move, JCBC-2075 ArrayInsert.createPath() deprecation, JCBC-1763 CollectionManager::getScope deprecation, JVMCBC-1530 QueryException deprecation, and many more). Only a curated, representative subset was extracted - facts with a clear Server-version gate (the round's stated priority), a clean cross-file corroboration opportunity with compatibility.json, or an unusually complete version-history arc (sdk:transaction-document-expiration's add/remove/re-add). Exhaustively extracting every changelog line across 2,800+ lines of release notes was judged to be reconciliation-scale work, not a single extraction record's job; the full changelog remains on the page for a future, more targeted pass (e.g. one extraction batch per SDK minor-version line) if the registry ever needs that level of granularity.

cross_component_finding: sdk:transaction-document-expiration's version history (availableSince 3.11.0 -> removedIn 3.11.1 -> availableSince 3.12.0) is the one clean example in this batch of a feature legitimately having TWO availableSince relations bracketing a removedIn relation for the same subject - not a contradiction, but a real add/regress/re-add arc that happened to be fully documented on a single page. Reconciliation should not treat two availableSince relations on one subject as automatically suspicious without checking for an intervening removedIn.
cross_product_finding: Three separate facts on this page independently corroborate compatibility.json's claim (same batch) that Java SDK 3.9.0 is a meaningful cross-language alignment point: the JVM clients BOM, the mono-versioning strategy statement, and (from compatibility.json) the API-version table's footnote that Scala/Kotlin adopted common release versions starting at Java 3.9/3.10. All three converge on version:sdk-3-9-0 as the point where Java's own release-numbering axis and the cross-SDK-family JVM alignment axis intersect, independently of the abstract cross-language 'SDK API' version axis (version:sdk-api-3-9) discussed in compatibility.json - three different axes, one coincidental release-number overlap worth flagging again here since it recurs.
